hook_text: You paid tax this week, even if you have never had a job. Check your till slip.
clip_script: A teacher's first payslip: before the salary lands, PAYE has gone to SARS. That is a direct tax, a tax on her income with her name on it. Then Saturday's till slip: maize meal, brown bread, milk, no VAT. Washing powder, a cooldrink, a charger: fifteen percent VAT added. Nobody from SARS sent her a bill; the shop collected it and pays it over later. That is an indirect tax. Here is the twist. A shopper earning four thousand rand pays about thirteen rand of every hundred in VAT. A shopper earning forty thousand pays about six and a half. Same rate, bigger bite for the poorer person. Economists call that regressive, and it is exactly why basic food is zero-rated.
visual_style: A whiteboard payslip with a PAYE line circled, then a till slip with VAT lines ticked and crossed, then two shoppers with a thirteen percent and a six and a half percent bubble.
mood: Surprising and fair-minded, a money reveal from everyday paper.
pacing: Quick payslip and till slip reveal, then a slower comparison of the two shoppers.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the VAT hiding in any price.
